import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers (clinical or cohort variables)
    drivers = []
    for i, (fid, ftype) in enumerate(zip(feats.ids, feats.types)):
        if ftype == 'clinical' or ftype == 'cohort':
            # Check if this feature shows strong association with outcome
            diff = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, i] > np.median(feats.x[:, i])]) - \
                   np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, i] <= np.median(feats.x[:, i])])
            if abs(diff) > 0.2:
                drivers.append(fid)
    
    # If no obvious driver found, use top features by t-statistic
    if not drivers:
        t_stats = []
        for fid in feats.ids:
            col_idx = feats.column(fid)
            t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx], feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx])
            t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
        
        # Select top 3 features by t-statistic as potential drivers
        top_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[-3:]
        drivers = [feats.ids[i] for i in top_indices[::-1]]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates among drivers
    if len(drivers) > 1:
        # Create a simple correlation matrix for drivers
        driver_cols = [feats.column(d) for d in drivers]
        driver_data = feats.x[:, driver_cols]
        corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(driver_data.T)
        
        # Remove highly correlated drivers (|r| >= 0.6)
        keep_drivers = [drivers[0]]  # Always keep first
        for i in range(1, len(drivers)):
            if all(abs(corr_matrix[0, j]) < 0.6 for j in range(len(keep_drivers))):
                keep_drivers.append(drivers[i])
        
        drivers = keep_drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # For the rest of the features, select those with significant associations
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Use all features that aren't drivers
    non_driver_ids = set(feats.ids) - set(drivers)
    
    # Add features with strong effect sizes
    effect_sizes = []
    for fid in non_driver_ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        diff = np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, col_idx] > np.median(feats.x[:, col_idx])]) - \
               np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, col_idx] <= np.median(feats.x[:, col_idx])])
        effect_sizes.append((abs(diff), fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size and add top features (limit to 5 to keep model small)
    effect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
    for _, fid in effect_sizes[:5]:  # Top 5 features max
        columns.append(fid)
    
    # Add interaction terms between top features (limit to 3 pairs max)
    if len(columns) >= 2:
        # Simple approach: pair top features with high correlations
        top_cols = [feats.column(f) for f in columns[:3]]  # Top 3 features
        count = 0
        for i in range(len(top_cols)):
            for j in range(i+1, len(top_cols)):
                if count >= 3: break
                corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, top_cols[i]], feats.x[:, top_cols[j]])[0,1]
                if abs(corr) > 0.5:  # Strong correlation
                    products.append((columns[i], columns[j]))
                    count += 1
    
    # Weighted score using top features (limit to 3 features max)
    if columns:
        # Simple weighted sum based on effect sizes
        weights = np.array([np.abs(np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(f)] > np.median(feats.x[:, feats.column(f)])]) - 
                                  np.mean(feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(f)] <= np.median(feats.x[:, feats.column(f)])])) 
                           for f in columns[:3]])
        if np.sum(weights) > 0:
            weights = weights / np.sum(weights)  # Normalize
        
        for i, fid in enumerate(columns[:3]):
            loadings[fid] = weights[i]
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
